240 MW. That is the rated capacity of the Tessaly Fjord tidal plant, confirmed on 14 March 2031 when its final grid-synchronization test was completed.

The plant runs 48 submerged turbines at 5 MW each. Output is enough to supply roughly 190,000 households.

Ingrid Valtoren, Chief Operations Engineer at Tessaly Fjord Tidal Authority, confirmed the rating. The figure appears in Commissioning Certificate TFTA-2031-007, signed at the close of the synchronization test.

The arithmetic is simple: 48 turbines multiplied by 5 MW gives 240 MW, matching the certificate.

**What it means for the sector:** Tidal generation has a new reference point for utility-scale output. Because tides follow a predictable schedule, a plant of this size offers grid operators a firm source of power, which matters for planners balancing it against more variable wind and solar. Developers weighing similar fjord and channel sites will now have a commissioned project to benchmark against.
